items.text: Adults 21 and over may possess up to 1 ounce (about 28 g) of cannabis leaf, up to 12 g of concentrate, or products holding up to 750 mg of THC, and may share it with another adult if no money changes hands. Using cannabis anywhere the public can access, or in a vehicle, is illegal. Home growing is not allowed.

Licensed adult-use sales began on 1 August 2025, first through converted medical cannabis centres; adult-use purchases carry a 15% tax. Visitors with a medical card from another state can apply at a Delaware medical dispensary for a Delaware card that runs to the same expiry date as their home card.

Package stores (bottle shops) may sell from 9 am to 1 am Monday to Saturday and from 10 am to 8 pm on Sunday; from October to December they may open at 8 am on Fridays and Saturdays. Package stores are closed on Thanksgiving, Christmas and Easter.

laws.rule: Delaware bans all drivers from using hand-held phones, tablets or laptops while driving, including talking without a hands-free device and reading, writing or sending texts or emails (21 Del. C. 4176C).
laws.penalty_signal: US$100 for a first offence; US$200 to US$300 for later offences (about A$142, and A$284 to A$426, at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026)

laws.rule: Using or consuming marijuana in an area accessible to the public, or in a moving vehicle, is an offence. 'Area accessible to the public' covers sidewalks, streets, alleys, parking lots, parks, playgrounds, stores, restaurants and other places the public is invited, and any outdoor spot within 10 feet of those or within 10 feet of the entrances, exits, opening windows or ventilation intakes of any public or private building. Cannabis stays illegal under US federal law, including on federal land.
laws.penalty_signal: unclassified misdemeanour: fine up to $200, up to 5 days in jail, or both
